sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's EV supply chain is structurally underpinned by nickel dominance and downstreaming mandates, making VKTR and TOBA prime beneficiaries of accelerating domestic adoption and export growth.
US utility resilience is driven by irreplaceable grid infrastructure demand from AI data centers and electrification, favoring PCG, EIX, and SRE with stable regulated returns.
Climate-tech divergence favors issuers with integrated renewable-plus-storage models (ESSA, CDIA) over pure-play volatility, as energy security and baseload reliability become investment priorities.
sectors.ai: Buy the dip in Indonesian EV/battery names (VKTR, TOBA) and resilient US utilities (PCG, EIX, SRE) on rate-cut tailwinds and domestic demand; rotate out of laggards with weak cash flow. Expect continued outperformance in ID-driven climate plays as policy support and electrification accelerate, while US names benefit from grid modernization and data-center load.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Election-cycle fiscal transfers and cash handouts are structurally boosting rural purchasing power, making mass-market FMCG and food staples the most durable demand pool through 2025.
Local-currency resilience and Bank Indonesia's rate-hold bias support consumer credit expansion, underpinning durable growth for mid-cap retailers and distributors with domestic revenue exposure.
The US consumer slowdown is a structural headwind for export-oriented FMCG producers, so long-term alpha lies in domestic-demand compounders, not global-supply-chain plays.
sectors.ai: Indonesia consumer/FMCG is a tactical WATCH: domestic names are ripping on local liquidity and election-driven consumption optimism, but US weakness caps conviction. Buy selective mid-cap winners (BRRC, COIN, JARR) on momentum, but trim into strength—the 0.93% aggregate masks a two-speed tape. Favor staples with pricing power and rural distribution; avoid export-linked names until global demand stabilizes.
